Step-up resolves the current bearer session, reserves a user-scoped TOTP anti-abuse slot, then performs all security checks in one PostgreSQL transaction: re-lock/recheck the auth session, lock the user, re-evaluate management-MFA eligibility, lock the current factor, require ACTIVE state, decrypt the factor secret with user+factor binding, verify the code strictly after any prior accepted time step, update last_accepted_step only while the factor is still ACTIVE, and establish assurance on the same session/factor at the same database operation time. This ordering fences concurrent logout/refresh replay/factor replacement and serializes TOTP replay. Verification failures are counted by anti-abuse; infrastructure/security-unavailable failures do not consume the bad-code budget.
feature_group: Management MFA TOTP step-up with replay and authority rechecks

review_notes: Login performs one Argon2 verification for every account state, using a fixed accepted dummy hash for unknown/passwordless/unsupported stored hashes and the real accepted hash otherwise. Only ACTIVE users with a supported matching password proceed. Before session issuance the transaction takes the per-user security advisory lock and rechecks the exact password hash plus ACTIVE status, fencing concurrent password/status changes. Access and refresh credentials are independent 256-bit random tokens; only domain-separated SHA-256 hashes are persisted. Session/access lifetime is 15 minutes bounded by a fixed 720-hour absolute session expiry, and the refresh expires at the same absolute boundary. Successful login finalizes any identifier anti-abuse reservation inside the same transaction so session creation cannot commit while limiter finalization fails. Refresh validates syntax, hashes the credential, obtains the same user security boundary, then locks refresh/session/user rows. A consumed refresh is treated as replay and atomically revokes the whole session family. Expired/revoked/disabled-user refresh likewise revokes the session. A valid refresh consumes the old credential, creates exactly one next-generation credential expiring at the unchanged absolute session deadline, links replaced_by_credential_id, rotates the access hash and clamps access/cookie lifetime to the absolute expiry. The old access token becomes stale because current_access_token_hash changes. Concurrent same-token refreshes therefore produce one winner and one replay revocation, intentionally invalidating the family after detected reuse.
feature_group: Staff password authentication, opaque session issuance and refresh-family rotation/replay revocation

Authorization/state/retry/transaction semantics therefore remain in the already-reviewed digital-collection-command path.
Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

The query binds organization and location together, applies Company default -> Location override with COALESCE for fee, payer, methods, tips, validation and release-payment policy, and returns Location currency. It takes FOR SHARE on both rows so a financial command sees a stable policy during its transaction. Runtime privilege provisioning grants SELECT plus UPDATE(updated_at) on organizations and locations, so this lock shape is compatible with the restricted runtime role and is not the SELECT-only lock failure seen on unrelated subscription data.
Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

Both routes set no-store headers and run through ApiOperationRunner guest operation classes. PATCH rejects nonempty query input, validates the body with paymentTipMutationRequestSchema, and delegates only through GuestCredentialAuthorizer with mutation=true before calling guestTip. GET validates an empty query and UUID-shaped session path, then authorizes a read credential before projecting the requested session. The controller never accepts organization/location/payment identifiers for the tip mutation and the response paths use explicit guest-safe projections.
feature_group: Guest payment tip mutation and safe payment projection HTTP routes

review_notes: Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

The helper writes one fixed PAYMENT_INITIALIZED Payment event with SYSTEM actor and canonical payment organization/location/session/entity identifiers. Metadata is limited to financial projection fields and contains no credential, provider secret or client-supplied raw payload. initialize-payment-command awaits this insert in the same transaction as canonical payment creation, so audit failure rolls the payment creation back.
Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

The closed four-code union distinguishes unavailable digital policy, creation-key conflict, invalid initialization and missing scope. Every code maps to a fixed safe message; the class preserves only the typed code/name and cannot leak SQL rows, policy internals or provider data.

parsePaymentBody delegates runtime validation to the supplied contract schema and parsePaymentUuid rejects non-UUID-shaped path values before storage access. Staff principal resolution requires a structurally valid rawHeaders array with exactly one Authorization header before resolving the bearer, preventing duplicate-header ambiguity. Response helpers serialize dates and project explicit contract-safe fields: guest mutation excludes payment IDs/internal timestamps, while shared projections include only the SafePaymentProjection contract; staff-only wrappers add payment/refund IDs.
feature_group: Payment transport parsing, staff principal resolution and response minimization

review_notes: Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

Input parsing accepts nonnegative canonical decimal strings with at most three fractional digits, converts exactly to bigint mills, and rejects values above the fixed maximum. Persisted parsing is intentionally more permissive about leading zeros but still bounded. parseCurrencyMoney adds currency minor-unit representability. formatMoney enforces nonnegative/bounded output and emits exactly three decimals. addMoney itself is a pure bigint sum; its only production consumer is payment-recompute, which immediately formats the derived amount and therefore re-applies the bound.
feature_group: Exact monetary parsing and formatting in thousandths

review_notes: The helper derives organization/location/session/payment identity from the locked MutablePayment and actor type from the trusted FinancialActor. Guest events deliberately store NULL membership plus actor_class=GUEST; staff events use MEMBERSHIP with the authorized membership ID. Currency/payment_id are always added to metadata and the insert is awaited by command callers inside their transaction. eventType/entityType/metadata are internal call parameters; inspected production callers use fixed event kinds and structured mutation metadata.
feature_group: Financial mutation audit append for tip/validation/corrections

review_notes: The ten-code closed union covers authorization denial, collection freeze, provider availability, amount/payment/tip/validation failures and precollection correction denial. All messages are fixed and resource authorization denial deliberately uses the generic requested-resource-not-available wording. The class carries no raw SQL/provider/request content.

assertCollectionNotStarted fails closed when canonical payment shows any paid amount, PENDING/PAID status, provider or provider reference, or repository-level collection evidence. It is invoked before guest/staff tip and precollection financial corrections/validation paths, preventing terms from changing after collection has begun even if the current payment row alone has not reached PAID.
feature_group: Freeze financial terms once collection evidence exists

review_notes: The repository locks the canonical payment by organization/location/session FOR UPDATE and validation history by organization/payment FOR UPDATE, serializing same-payment mutations. Collection evidence checks any cash entry, provider event or durable collection operation, so even an incomplete/failed collection attempt freezes mutable financial terms. Validation replacement clears only the currently locked prior row before inserting the new current row. updatePaymentTerms rewrites precollection terms and clears provider/reference/paidAt from a trusted locked payment; callers first enforce collection-not-started and recompute exact money. projectMutation returns the bounded mutation view.
feature_group: Canonical payment mutation locking, validation history and persistence

review_notes: Types separate trusted PaymentScope, canonical MutablePayment, validation history, recomputed state and public-service mutation projection. FinancialActor is limited to GUEST or LOCATION_MANAGER; guest membership is nullable while manager callers supply a membership. The declarations do not themselves enforce runtime coherence, so authority and state correctness remain with the reviewed service/repository/commands.
feature_group: Typed financial mutation scope, actor and projection contracts

review_notes: Every manager mutation opens one payment transaction, authorizes an active LOCATION_MANAGER against the exact session/location and then locks the canonical payment, resolves effective policy and server operation time before invoking validation/tip/correction commands. Guest tip re-resolves and locks the guest credential/session inside the same transaction; invalid access is counted for anti-abuse, valid domain rejection/success finalizes as ignored, and unexpected failures roll back. Guest callers cannot select organization/location/payment identity.
feature_group: Manager and guest financial mutation transaction orchestration

review_notes: Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

The query operates on an already-authorized ProjectionScope, locks the session and payment scope for a stable read, resolves the current release-payment policy, then loads only the current validation and ordered refund history for that canonical payment. Internal provider/reference fields are read solely to compute fail-closed release satisfaction and are not included in SafeProjectionPayment. With no payment, release is satisfied only when policy does not require payment.
feature_group: Safe payment/refund projection and release-payment status

review_notes: The service-level projection deliberately omits provider/reference, refund reason/provider/idempotency and tenant identifiers. It includes payment/refund IDs and internal Dates for staff-capable consumers, while guest HTTP projection separately strips those IDs and internal timestamps. Current validation exposes only amount and controlled mode.

Staff reads authorize the exact session against active staff membership/location access; non-manager employee/supervisor reads additionally require current shift operational eligibility. Guest reads re-resolve and lock the credential, require its canonical session id to equal the requested path session, then load the safe projection in the same transaction. Invalid/cross-session guest reads consume anti-abuse budget and return the same GuestAccessError shape.

The function parses persisted service/tip/validation as exact mills, rejects validation greater than service, subtracts validation only when the customer pays service, and always adds the tip. Zero due converges to NONE/NOT_REQUIRED. For positive due, recomputePayment directly rejects DIGITAL_ONLY; separately, this baseline wires an UnconfiguredDigitalPaymentProviderRegistry. Other positive policies converge to CASH/UNPAID. Mutation callers invoke collection-freeze guards before persisting this recomputation.

Closed unions define payer, methods, collection method and five payment statuses. EffectiveFinancialPolicy mirrors the authoritative configuration fields. PaymentProjection is intentionally internal and includes creation idempotency, provider/reference and tenant/session identity; public controllers consume narrower projection functions rather than serializing it directly.
Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

The audit event binds canonical payment organization/location/session to an EXTERNAL_PROVIDER actor and records only provider, normalized result kind, payment id, operation/refund id and optional normalized safe result code. Entity/event type are selected from the closed authenticated event subject/kind. provider-event-ingress appends this only after an authoritative reconciliation and event persistence inside the same transaction.

Reconciliation first resolves the operation only within the authenticated provider binding organization, locks the related session/payment/operation, and requires an unresolved dispatched state, matching provider, compatible stable reference, exact currency/amount snapshot, zero paid amount, null paidAt and UNPAID/FAILED payment. A provider reference must be present and unowned elsewhere. The operation CAS to RESOLVED and guarded payment projection to PAID/FAILED occur in one transaction; a failed payment update throws so the operation transition rolls back. Reordered failures cannot downgrade PAID, PREPARED/REJECTED/RESOLVED operations cannot revive, and a definitive failure permits a later fresh guarded collection attempt.

The callback boundary exposes only rejected versus processing-failed outcomes with fixed messages. Provider transport/authenticator exceptions are collapsed to REJECTED and post-auth reconciliation/storage failures are collapsed to PROCESSING_FAILED by provider-event-ingress, preventing SQL/provider internals from leaking through this domain error.
Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

Refund callback authority begins from the authenticated binding organization, resolves only that tenant's refund/payment, locks the session/payment/refund, and accepts transitions only from PENDING with null completedAt and matching provider/reference. Success requires a provider reference; a non-null reference must not belong to another refund. The guarded UPDATE moves the refund once to SUCCEEDED with completedAt or FAILED without completedAt and never rewrites the canonical payment collection facts.

Committed-event dedup is keyed by authenticated organization/provider/providerEventId. Collection/refund correlation lookup is tenant scoped before identities are exposed. Reconciliation locks the related ValetSession, then payment FOR UPDATE and the operation/refund FOR UPDATE, while reference-ownership queries prevent reusing a provider reference across same-tenant collection/payment or refunds. Event persistence stores only normalized provider identity/event id/reference/status/safe result code and canonical payment/refund linkage.
feature_group: Provider event deduplication, tenant correlation and reconciliation locks

review_notes: The discriminated union separates collection and refund subjects and constrains financial outcomes to collection success/failure/no-change or refund success/failure. Authority is explicitly split into an authenticator-supplied organization/provider binding and a normalized event; raw callback fields are not themselves an authority type. Processing results expose only dedup/persistence/status identifiers.

The validator accepts only a canonical UUID organization binding, bounded trimmed provider/event/reference text, a closed event kind, bounded provider event id, restricted safeResultCode and canonical UUID subject id. Refund success and financial collection success/failure require a provider reference; only NO_FINANCIAL_CHANGE and refund failure may omit it. It reconstructs a fresh normalized object, dropping unrelated authenticator/raw fields.
Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

The audit binds canonical payment organization/location/session and the authorized manager membership to a fixed PAYMENT_REFUND_CREATED Refund entity. Metadata is limited to amount, currency, collection method, payment/refund ids and initial refund status; free-form refund reason and idempotency key are deliberately omitted. The insert omits actor_type because the audit foundation BEFORE INSERT trigger normalizes a non-null actor_membership_id with null actor_type to MEMBERSHIP.
Retained original published status; no new semantic-review claim.

The closed error contract exposes only invalid amount, idempotency conflict and refund-not-allowed with fixed messages. Authorization denial is intentionally supplied by the shared financial authorization error before refund-specific processing.

Idempotency lookup is tenant scoped and returns immutable refund identity for exact-retry comparison. Refundable exposure sums only PENDING and SUCCEEDED rows, so definitive failures release balance while still retaining history. New rows persist canonical payment/tenant, authorized membership, opaque idempotency key, normalized amount/reason/provider and server operation time. Public RefundProjection excludes membership, tenant/payment ids, idempotency, provider/reference and reason.
feature_group: Refund idempotency lookup, exposure accounting and insert/projection

review_notes: Refund state is intentionally independent from ValetSession custody: PENDING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED records persist as financial history, while the safe service projection exposes only amount/currency/id/timestamps/status. PersistedRefund carries authority/idempotency/provider/reason fields for internal comparison/reconciliation.
feature_group: Refund lifecycle and safe projection types

review_notes: Refund money uses exact bigint mills with canonical external syntax, a persisted-money mode and a fixed maximum. requireRepresentableRefund requires positive amount and currency minor-unit compatibility. Request validation requires canonical UUID actor/session ids, bounded nonblank/control-free idempotency key, and normalizeRefundReason trims then bounds the reason to 500 code points without controls. The idempotency key is intentionally treated as opaque rather than trimmed/canonicalized.
feature_group: Refund request identity, exact money and reason validation

review_notes: The injectable constructs one createRefundExecutor from the restricted runtime pool and forwards only authenticated staff user/session scope plus the validated RefundRequest. Authorization, payment locking, collected-state proof, exposure accounting, idempotency and atomic audit semantics all remain in refund-command.
feature_group: Refund service facade over restricted runtime executor

review_notes: Every route runs through a named ApiOperationRunner operation, resolves the authenticated principal with duplicate-Authorization protection, parses the path session as UUID and validates each request body against its contract before entering payment/refund/cash services. The controller supplies only authenticated user plus path session scope; deeper services re-authorize location/role/state. Responses pass explicit payment/cash/refund/staff projection functions rather than serializing internal rows.
feature_group: Staff payment projection, refund, cash and financial mutation HTTP routes

review_notes: Validation mutation requires the effective policy to enable validation and the customer to be the service payer. It locks validation history, normalizes FULL/NONE/PARTIAL with exact currency math, treats an identical current validation as an idempotent no-op, rejects NONE without a current row, then enforces collection-not-started before inserting/superseding validation, recomputing payment terms and appending audit in the same transaction. Historical rows remain immutable while is_current moves to the new record.

ROI capture owns every raw/cropped URI until exactly one validated, size-bounded cropped JPEG is handed to the OCR loop. It sends generation/mount/revision metadata into native capture, requires returned metadata identity and preview dimensions to match, derives crop only from validated native transform, retries compression without recapturing, and cleans all other files on every exit.

Crop adapter uses ImageManipulator for one explicit ROI crop and returns a wrapper that can save JPEG at caller-selected quality while ensuring both rendered image and manipulation context are released. It does not infer crop coordinates or retain base64 data.

Failure module defines a closed native/capture diagnostic reason set and converts native error codes only when they match the OCR_CAPTURE_METADATA_ namespace. Rotation detail is retained only for a recognized rotation diagnostic code; user-facing Error text stays generic.

File helper exposes only existence/size inspection and deletion for transient OCR paths. removePlateFile retries a failed deletion once, logs only a closed cleanup classification, and still fails the operation after any initial deletion failure even if the second attempt succeeds.

Geometry code validates finite positive layout/image dimensions, exact generation/mount/revision identity, exact captured image dimensions, and an invertible affine 3x3 preview-to-image transform. It maps all four guide corners, rejects out-of-bounds/degenerate results, then adds a bounded 10% crop margin clamped to actual pixels.

Metadata boundary isolates version-specific native camera extensions. Preview metadata requires positive safe dimensions and a valid affine sensorToView matrix; capture metadata requires safe generation/mount/revision and positive preview/image dimensions plus a valid affine previewToImage matrix, with missing/invalid capture metadata classified explicitly.

Forward-only hardening closes NULL-as-clear on primary-color SET and normalizes existing display-name overrides before replacing the check with canonical outer-trim enforcement. Dedicated CLEAR remains the only supported override removal path.

Defines staff push registrations, tenant/session/task-scoped intents and deliveries with registration/delivery state-machine guards, lease fencing, retry bounds, terminal shapes and dedupe indexes. Registration rows are account-session scoped rather than tenant scoped; the delivery writer and worker eligibility query bind the registration's staff-auth user back to the exact recipient membership, organization, location access and active shift before any provider send.

Adds bounded SKIP LOCKED cleanup for terminal deliveries, orphaned old intents and terminal registrations, with dependency checks preventing deletion of still-referenced rows. Cleanup is SECURITY DEFINER with fixed search_path and PUBLIC execution revoked; runtime provisioning explicitly controls cleanup execution.

Extends tenant audit events with typed actor provenance and introduces a separate append-only account-security audit stream. The audit actor CHECK is deliberately NOT VALID so legacy null-actor history remains readable, while PostgreSQL still enforces it for new/updated rows; investigation queries explicitly preserve legacy null-as-membership semantics. Account-security append uses a stable-id advisory lock and exact idempotent replay comparison.

Adds protected TOTP factor state, ten-slot versioned recovery-code sets and exact-session MFA assurance fields. DB guards make factor identity/secret immutable, prevent ACTIVE->PENDING or RETIRED reactivation, enforce monotonically advancing accepted TOTP steps and recovery generation, and make recovery verifiers immutable except one-way consumption.

Later LM-authority/onboarding migrations CREATE OR REPLACE these three commands, so current behavior was checked against the replacement chain rather than treating this historical body as final.

Organization advisory serialization precedes row/CAS mutation, company-default fee changes validate every inheriting location's currency precision, location overrides preserve Company->Location precedence, operating hours require exactly seven distinct weekdays and valid same-day intervals, and audit captures canonical old/new values. The migration also strengthens existing LM configuration/branding helpers with the same organization settings lock.
